# filmopen_store

*Generated by `scripts/package_digest.py`; regenerate, never edit.*

Where a project's files come from and how they are written, as pure Dart: the folder source (`directory_source*.dart`, `dart:io` behind a stub), the loader, **the writer** (`project_writer.dart`) with its refusals, the creator and the template, `Guards` (development mode's policy), the log (`app_log.dart`, `log_file*.dart`) and the library install.

**pure Dart.** 27 files, 4,740 lines under `lib/`; 568 tests in 50 files. Barrel: `lib/filmopen_store.dart`.

## Depends on

- **filmopen_format** — uses `AllocatedId`, `AllocationInventory`, `Author`, `BatchStem`, `ChildEntry`, `Commentary`, `CommentaryStem`, `DuplicateKeyException`, `Entity`, `EntityGroup`, `EntityOrigin`, `EntityType`, `EntityVersions`, `EpochDeclaration`, `FileMedia`, `FileNameParser`, `FilmProject`, `MediaLocation`, `NotJsonObjectException`, `OfficialPointer`, `OfficialStem`, `ProjectArea`, `ProjectManifest`, `ProjectSource`, `ProjectWarning`, `PromptPath`, `PromptState`, `RenderBatch`, `SetRecord`, `ShortName` and 59 more
- **filmopen_test_support (dev)** — uses nothing by name the digest could see

Third-party: crypto.

## Used by

`filmopen_account`, `filmopen_app`, `filmopen_assistant_ui`, `filmopen_automation`, `filmopen_browser`, `filmopen_cloud`, `filmopen_compare`, `filmopen_device`, `filmopen_dictation`, `filmopen_drive`, `filmopen_engine`, `filmopen_engine_bench`, `filmopen_engine_mlt`, `filmopen_engine_mpv`, `filmopen_exchange`, `filmopen_fdx`, `filmopen_forms`, `filmopen_insertion`, `filmopen_insertion_ui`, `filmopen_jobs_ui`, `filmopen_keys`, `filmopen_machine`, `filmopen_media_ui`, `filmopen_picker`, `filmopen_platform`, `filmopen_plugin_host`, `filmopen_plugins_ui`, `filmopen_prompt_ui`, `filmopen_recorder`, `filmopen_relay`, `filmopen_render_ui`, `filmopen_sharing`, `filmopen_state`, `filmopen_support`, `filmopen_test_support`, `filmopen_timeline`, `filmopen_timeline_ui`, `filmopen_tree`

## Public API

What the barrel exports, file by file. A name is `class`, `enum`, `mixin`, `extension`, `typedef`, a top-level function, getter, setter or variable; under a class, its public constructors, fields, getters, setters and methods.

### `lib/src/app_log.dart`

- **enum `LogLevel`** — Verbosity, least to most.
  - values: `error`, `warning`, `info`, `debug`, `trace`
  - `static LogLevel? fromName(String name)`
- **class `LogEntry`** — One line of the log.
  - `LogEntry(this.level, this.event, {this.data = const {}, this.error, this.stackTrace, DateTime? time})`
  - `final DateTime time`
  - `final LogLevel level`
  - `final String event` — A stable dotted name, e.g. `project.opened`, `render.failed`.
  - `final Map<String, Object?> data` — Structured detail.
  - `final Object? error`
  - `final StackTrace? stackTrace`
  - `Map<String, Object?> toJson()`
  - `String toLine()` — The JSON line, without its newline.
- **class `LogSink`** — Where log lines go.
  - `void write(LogEntry entry)`
  - `Future<void> close()` — Flushes and releases resources.
- **class `MemoryLogSink`** — Keeps entries in memory, for tests.
  - `final List<LogEntry> entries`
- **class `LineLogSink`** — Hands each line to a callback: the console, a test.
  - `const LineLogSink(this.onLine)`
  - `final void Function(String line) onLine`
- **class `AppLog`** — The application log.
  - `AppLog({this.threshold = LogLevel.info})`
  - `static final AppLog instance`
  - `static String digestOf(String value)` — The first 12 hexadecimal characters of the SHA-256 of [value]'s UTF-8: a short, stable identifier made from a value.
  - `LogLevel threshold` — Entries above this level are dropped before reaching any sink.
  - `bool thresholdPinned` — True when the environment (`FILMOPEN_LOG_LEVEL`) fixed the threshold.
  - `void pinThreshold(LogLevel level)` — Fixes [threshold] for the run; see [thresholdPinned].
  - `void applyVerbose(bool verbose)` — Applies the *verbose logs* setting unless the environment pinned a level.
  - `void forceVerbose(bool on, {required String reason})` — Verbose while a recording runs, [on] at its start and off at its end, whatever the setting says (§6.8): in memory only, so the setting and the preferences are never touched and a crash leaves nothing to undo.
  - `String? filePath` — Where the file sink writes, when one is attached; shown in Settings.
  - `List<LogSink> get sinks`
  - `void addSink(LogSink sink)`
  - `void removeSink(LogSink sink)`
  - `bool isEnabled(LogLevel level)`
  - `void log(LogLevel level, String event, {Map<String, Object?> data = const {}, Object? error, StackTrace? stackTrace})`
  - `void error(String event, {Map<String, Object?> data = const {}, Object? error, StackTrace? stackTrace})`
  - `void warning(String event, {Map<String, Object?> data = const {}, Object? error})`
  - `void info(String event, {Map<String, Object?> data = const {}})`
  - `void debug(String event, {Map<String, Object?> data = const {}})`
  - `void trace(String event, {Map<String, Object?> data = const {}})`
  - `Future<T> timed<T>(String event, Future<T> Function() body, {LogLevel level = LogLevel.debug, Map<String, Object?> data = const {}})` — Runs [body], logging how long it took.
  - `Future<void> close()`

### `lib/src/guards.dart`

- **enum `GuardRule`** — A refusal the development switch governs.
  - values: `notYourFile`, `notDirector`, `libraryFile`
- **class `Guards`** — The policy the writer consults before refusing a [GuardRule].
  - `const Guards({this.warnOnly = false})`
  - `static const Guards enforce` — Every guard refuses: a release build, and any caller that did not ask.
  - `static const Guards warn` — Development mode: a governed guard warns instead of refusing.
  - `final bool warnOnly`
  - `void check(GuardRule rule, Exception Function() refusal, {Map<String, Object?> data = const {}})` — Throws what [refusal] makes when enforcing, after logging `guard.refused`; in development mode lets it through.
  - `void report(Iterable<GuardRule> rules, {Map<String, Object?> data = const {}})` — Logs `guard.overridden` for each rule a write went ahead in spite of, with [data] — the viewer and the file.

### `lib/src/project_writer.dart`

- **class `NoManifestException`** — A manifest write requires an existing project manifest (§4.4).
  - `const NoManifestException()`
- **class `NoSelectedProjectException`** — Declaring an epoch requires the project version in use for the viewer (§8.2).
  - `const NoSelectedProjectException()` — Refuses a missing project file or an unresolved choice between project versions.
- **class `EpochSourceUnavailableException`** — Creating at a missing epoch requires a resolved version at the chosen source epoch.
  - `const EpochSourceUnavailableException(this.groupKey, this.epoch)` — Refuses a missing group, source epoch or viewer resolution without choosing another source.
  - `final String groupKey` — The canonical entity group whose source could not be resolved.
  - `final String epoch` — The explicitly chosen source epoch.
- **class `OutfitParentUnavailableException`** — A new outfit requires an existing character group in the project or library.
  - `const OutfitParentUnavailableException(this.character)` — Refuses an absent character without copying or creating its parent.
  - `final String character` — The complete character tag whose group is missing.
- **class `EpochDeclaredPickFailedException`** — The declared epoch exists in a new project fork, but selecting that fork failed.
  - `const EpochDeclaredPickFailedException(this.epoch, this.stem)` — Reports partial completion without undoing the fork or allocating another epoch.
  - `final String epoch` — The allocated token already written into the fork's declarations.
  - `final VersionStem stem` — The existing project fork the caller can recover after refreshing.
- **class `ProjectReadOnlyException`** — The project's files cannot be written (bundled assets).
  - `const ProjectReadOnlyException(this.label)`
  - `final String label`
- **class `NotYourFileException`** — The file belongs to another author; edit a fork instead (§17 rule 2).
  - `const NotYourFileException(this.stem, this.owner, this.viewer)`
  - `final String stem`
  - `final Author owner` — Who the file belongs to.
  - `final Author? viewer`
- **class `NotYourTakeException`** — A take another author made, whose file is theirs (§9.0): its entry's flag stands, its file stays.
  - `const NotYourTakeException(super.stem, super.owner, super.viewer)`
- **class `TakeStillNamedException`** — A take whose file a live entry of another document still names (§9.0): only the entry's flag stands.
  - `const TakeStillNamedException(this.reference, this.documents)`
  - `final String reference` — The take's stem.
  - `final List<String> documents` — The stems of the documents whose live entries name it.
- **class `NoViewerException`** — Writing without a viewer handle: there is no author to write as.
  - `const NoViewerException()`
- **class `NotDirectorException`** — Only a director of the project writes official pointers (§8.3, §13.2).
  - `const NotDirectorException(this.viewer)`
  - `final Author? viewer`
- **class `IdentityChangedException`** — A save tried to change what names the file (§7): `filmopen`, `type`, `tag`, `epoch`, `author` or `v`.
  - `const IdentityChangedException(this.key)`
  - `final String key`
- **class `NextEpochLoweredException`** — A save refused because it would lower, drop or spoil a project file's `next_epoch`.
  - `const NextEpochLoweredException(this.floor)` — The refusal, naming the [floor] the file holds.
  - `final num floor` — The floor the file holds.
- **class `EntityExistsException`** — A new entity was asked for under a tag its type already has.
  - `const EntityExistsException(this.groupKey)`
  - `final String groupKey` — `<type>_<tag>`, e.g. `ch_main-hero`.
- **class `DiscardOfficialException`** — A version official names, or the project file of record, was asked to be discarded (§6.1, §4.1): the director moves or clears the star first.
  - `const DiscardOfficialException(this.stem)`
  - `final String stem` — The version's stem.
- **class `PluginOutputException`** — What a plug-in's entity hook returned cannot be written (§14.4).
  - `const PluginOutputException(this.code)`
  - `final String code`
- **class `PluginRun`** — A plug-in's run, as its files record it (Project Specification §12.4, §14.4).
  - `const PluginRun({required this.tag, required this.stem, required this.hook, this.settings, this.item = const {}})`
  - `final String tag`
  - `final String stem`
  - `final String hook`
  - `final Map<String, Object?>? settings` — The project-scoped settings the run had, for an entity hook: its batch records them, empty where it had none (§12.4).
  - `final Map<String, Object?> item` — What a render's record says it was asked (§12.2): its `request`, **as the application prepared it**, and from the plug-in's answer `stack`, `seed_applied: false`, `metadata` and `metadata_refused`, which the record ke…
  - `Author runner(Author viewer)` — The handle the run's files are written under (§5.6, §14.4).
- **variable** `const List<String> identityKeys` — The header fields that must equal the filename's (§7).
- **enum `ContentProblem`** — What a file must say to be worth writing (§7, §8.2, §18.3).
  - values: `nameRequired`, `versionLabelTooLong`, `epochsRequired`, `childrenNotAList`, `folderIntoItself`, `childListedTwice`
- **class `ForkSourceUnreadableException`** — A fork's source could not be read to check it against the text it was read as; the fork was not written.
  - `const ForkSourceUnreadableException(super.path)`
- **class `InvalidContentException`**
  - `const InvalidContentException(this.problem)`
  - `final ContentProblem problem`
- **function** `void validateContent(EntityType type, Map<String, dynamic> json)` — Refuses content the format requires otherwise.
- **class `RecordedWrite`** — One write a [ProjectWriter] made or is making: the source it went to, the path, and the text, null for a deletion.
  - `final ProjectSource root` — The source written: the project's, or the library's for a development-mode save of a library entity (§9.5).
  - `final String path` — The path within [root].
  - `final String? text` — What the write put there; null where it deleted the file.
  - `bool landed` — Whether the source has answered the write; until then it is in flight.
- **class `WriteRecord`** — What the app is writing and has written since the index last took it (§7.5).
  - `RecordedWrite begin(ProjectSource root, String path, String? text)` — Enters a write of [text] (null: a deletion) at [path] in [root], in flight.
  - `void land(RecordedWrite write)` — Marks [write] landed: the source answered it.
  - `void drop(RecordedWrite write, {bool stale = false})` — Removes [write], refused or failed; [stale] keeps its path for the next publication to read again.
  - `void markStale(ProjectSource root, String path)` — Keeps [path] in [root], which a check found changed since it was read, for the next publication to read again.
  - `List<RecordedWrite> takeLanded([Iterable<ProjectSource>? roots])` — The landed writes in the order they were entered, removed from the record; those in flight stay.
  - `List<RecordedWrite> landedOf(Iterable<ProjectSource> roots)` — The landed writes of [roots] in the order they were entered, left in the record: what a decision lays over the published index (§7.5).
  - `void release(List<RecordedWrite> writes)` — Removes [writes], which a publication has laid into the index it published.
  - `List<(ProjectSource, String)> takeStale()` — The paths stale refusals named since the last call, removed from the record.
  - `bool hasNews([Iterable<ProjectSource>? roots])` — Whether a publication has anything to take: a landed write or a stale path, of [roots] where given.
  - `Set<String> pathsOf(ProjectSource root)` — The paths of [root] the record names, landed or in flight: a re-derivation does not read them.
  - `String? landedText(ProjectSource root, String path)` — The text of the last landed write at [path] in [root], which the index may not hold yet.
  - `RecordedWrite? latest(ProjectSource root, String path)` — The last write entered for [path] in [root], landed or in flight; null where the record names none.
- **class `ProjectWriter`** — Writes guarded project documents through the source of an immutable project snapshot.
  - `ProjectWriter(this.project, {this.guards = Guards.enforce, this.record})`
  - `final FilmProject project`
  - `final WriteRecord? record` — Where each write is entered before the source is asked, for the index to take (§7.5).
  - `Map<String, dynamic>? get written` — The document this writer's last save, create or fork wrote, as written; null before one landed.
  - `final Guards guards` — Whether the rules about who may write warn instead of refusing (development mode, §9.5).
  - `Future<void> updateManifest(Map<String, Object?> Function(Map<String, Object?> json) change, {required Author? viewer})` — Changes the manifest as the viewer, against the text the index read, refusing a concurrent edit (§6.1).
  - `static const notContent` — What a file holds beside its content (§7): a change to these alone does not move `updated`.
  - `static const blockNotContent` — What a block holds beside its content (§10.3): its takes, the seconds the scene's output gives it, its own time.
  - `Future<Entity> saveEntity(Entity entity, Map<String, dynamic> json, {required Author? viewer})` — Replaces the content of [entity]'s file with [json], setting `updated` where the content changed (§7).
  - `void checkSave(Entity entity, Map<String, dynamic> json, {required Author? viewer})` — Whether [saveEntity] would refuse [json] as the new content of [entity].
  - `Future<VersionStem> fork(Entity entity, {required Author? viewer, Map<String, dynamic>? content, String? draftLabel})` — Copies [entity] as the viewer's own next version (§13.1), holding [content] where given, and returns its stem.
  - `Future<String> declareEpoch(String label, {int? year, required Author? viewer})` — Appends an allocated epoch to the viewer's project version in use and returns its token (§8.2).
  - `Future<String> relabelEpoch(String tag, String label, {int? year, required Author? viewer})` — Gives the declared epoch [tag] of the viewer's project version in use a new label and year, and returns its token.
  - `Future<VersionStem> createAtEpoch(EntityGroup group, String targetEpoch, {required String sourceEpoch, required Author? viewer, bool clear = false,…` — Copies a character or location's exact resolved source into a declared missing epoch as the viewer's v1.
  - `Future<VersionStem> createOutfit(String character, String epoch, String name, {required Author? viewer, String? draftLabel})` — Creates a named outfit under an allocated owner identity for an existing character (§9.2).
  - `Future<VersionStem> createEntity({ required EntityType type, required String tag, String? epoch, required String name, String? kind, required Autho…` — Writes a new entity as the viewer's first version (§9, §10, §13.1).
  - `Future<List<String>> writePluginRun({ required PluginRun run, required List<Entity> sources, required List<Map<String, dynamic>> outputs, required…` — Writes what a plug-in's entity hook returned (Project Specification §14.4, §12.4, §5.6).
  - `static const renderRequestRequired` — The members a render record's `request` must hold (§12.2); the others are written where known.
  - `static const renderRequestOptional` — The members a render record's `request` may hold beside [renderRequestRequired].
  - `Future<bool> setDiscarded(Entity entity, {required bool discarded, required Author? viewer})` — Sets [entity] aside with `discarded`, or brings it back by removing the key (Project Specification §7, §6.1).
  - `Future<SetRecord> writeSet(SetRecord record, {required Author? viewer})` — Writes a pending set's record — a comp, an assistant session or a render queue (Project Specification §12.7).
  - `Future<RenderBatch> writeImportBatch({ required BatchStem stem, required List<Map<String, dynamic>> items, required Author? viewer, Map<String, dyn…` — Writes the record of one import action, or of one render (§12.2, §12.3).
  - `({String choice, bool landed})? inUseRecorded(Entity entity, {required Author? viewer})` — The recorded choice, in flight or landed and unpublished, that makes [entity] the version in use, or null.
  - `Future<void> setOfficial(Entity entity, {required Author? viewer})` — Writes the official pointer for [entity]'s versions key (§13.2) naming it, with `set_by` and `set_at`.
  - `Future<void> clearOfficial(Entity entity, {required Author? viewer})` — Removes the official pointer for [entity]'s versions key, so the project has no chosen version there.
  - `Future<void> setPick(EntityVersions versions, {required Author? viewer, Entity? entity, bool trackOfficial = false})` — Records the viewer's pick at [versions]' epoch (§13.4).
  - `Future<bool> visit(Entity entity, {required Author? viewer, DateTime? now})` — Records when the viewer last had [entity]'s media on screen (§13.4 `visited`): [now], or this second.
  - `Future<bool> deleteTake(String reference, {required Author? viewer})` — Deletes the file of the take [reference] names, and its thumbnail (§9.0).

### `lib/src/usage_log.dart`

- **class `UsageLogUnavailable`** — A usage log that could not do what was asked, with a code.
  - `const UsageLogUnavailable(this.code)`
  - `final String code`
- **class `UsageReading`** — What a reading of the log found (§6.7, *Reading*).
  - `const UsageReading({this.records = const [], this.skippedChains = const {}, this.complete = true})`
  - `final List<UsageRecord> records` — Every record read, in file and line order.
  - `final Set<String> skippedChains` — The chains holding a record of a version this reader does not know, left out whole.
  - `final bool complete` — False when a month file could not be read, so that a total can say it may be short.
  - `List<UsageChain> get chains` — The calls read.
  - `static void addLines(String file, Iterable<String> lines, { required List<UsageRecord> records, required Set<String> skippedChains, required Set<St…` — Reads the [lines] of the month file [file] into [records] and [skippedChains].
- **class `UsageLog`** — Where usage records go (§6.7).
  - `const UsageLog()`
  - `static UsageLog current` — The log in use.
  - `static void install(UsageLog log)` — Makes [log] the one in use.
  - `bool get isAvailable` — Whether records can be written at all.
  - `Future<String> deviceId()` — The id in the usage folder's `device.json`, which is made on first use.
  - `Future<void> append(UsageRecord record)` — Appends [record], or throws [UsageLogUnavailable].
  - `Future<UsageReading> read()` — Every record in the log.
  - `Stream<void> get changes` — An event after each record this app appends.
  - `Future<void> appendUntilWritten(UsageRecord record, {Duration firstWait = const Duration(milliseconds: 250)})`
- **class `UnavailableUsageLog`** — No usage log: nothing is written, so no paid call starts.
  - `const UnavailableUsageLog()`
- **class `MemoryUsageLog`** — A usage log in memory, for the tests and the agent build, which must not write the user's usage folder.
  - `MemoryUsageLog({this.device = '00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000000'})`
  - `final String device` — The id [deviceId] answers.
  - `final List<String> lines` — The lines written, oldest first, without their line feeds.
  - `int failing` — How many of the next appends fail, as a write that cannot take the lock fails.
  - `List<UsageRecord> get records` — The records written.

- `lib/src/directory_source_stub.dart`: `canOpenDirectories`, `directoryProjectSource`, `directoryExists`, `osErrorCodeOf`
- `lib/src/library_install_io.dart`: `installLibraryIfEmpty`
- `lib/src/log_file_io.dart`: `FileLogSink`, `openFileLogSink`
